title: Vendor starts
text: Zamp makes vendor onboarding a clear handoff between the supplier, procurement, and the assigned reviewer. This is a fictional practice account. The sample details belong to this company, and its required proof is uploaded with the form. The vendor still reviews the information and makes the declarations before submitting.

title: Submission
text: The review screen brings the business details, document checklist, and declarations together. Submission runs the checks and saves an application reference. The vendor can see the current stage and who acts next, rather than wondering whether the application disappeared.

title: Procurement routes work
text: Procurement sees the organisation's applications and assigns the decision maker. This role coordinates invitations and handoffs. It does not approve vendors. A reviewer can access only the cases currently assigned to them, even through a copied link.

title: Reviewer decides
text: The assigned reviewer opens the case, checks its evidence and readiness, and records the human decision. Automated checks support the review; they do not replace it. Known blockers and incomplete verification prevent approval, and competing stale decisions cannot overwrite the saved result.

title: Vendor receives decision
text: The vendor receives an in-app approval notice that opens the decision receipt. The receipt includes the application reference and decision date, and confirms that no application tasks remain. Onboarding approval is separate from purchasing access or payment activation. Email delivery is not implemented in this prototype.

title: A specific correction
text: Here is the edge case. The bank account entered on the form differs from the uploaded cheque. The vendor sees both the problem and the requested next step. They can correct the requested value or replace the requested proof. Earlier evidence stays on record. This response corrects the number to match the cheque.

title: Reviewer sees the reply
text: The reviewer's queue now identifies the vendor reply. Opening the case shows what changed and the vendor's explanation, before the reviewer enters the detailed evidence workspace. A reply alone does not approve the application. Each outstanding request still needs assessment, and the original and replacement evidence remain traceable.

title: Scope and limits
text: This walkthrough uses synthetic documents and independent simulated registry records. Unknown identifiers stay unverified. The test workbook records expected and observed outcomes, including deliberate errors. The hosted demonstration uses a free service, so it can sleep and its temporary data can reset. The submission evidence should be read with those limits in mind.
